cards.name: Instagram feed post caption
cards.summary: The text under an Instagram feed photo, video or carousel: up to 2,200 characters and 20 @ tags, but a good one is built for its first line, a short body, at most 5 hashtags and one clear action. The cap is a ceiling, never a target.
use_for: Captions for brand feed posts (a Pune D2C launch, a Jaipur CA firm's GST-deadline reminder)
The single caption that sits under a whole carousel (slide 1 carries the hook, the caption carries the searchable phrase)
Captions for Reels and partnership or creator posts, where the disclosure must be visible
Event, giveaway and recap posts that need rules or details in plain text
avoid: A block of 15-30 hashtags. The Help Center cap is 5 (see plat:instagram_hashtags); the API reference still prints 30 and is stale. Write to 5.

A URL as the call to action. Links in captions are not clickable [UNVERIFIED: general platform knowledge, not read from a platform page on 2026-10-04]. Say 'link in bio', give a DM keyword, or use the ad's button.
Opening with greetings or throat-clearing ('Hello friends, hope you are well'). Whatever sits above the 'more' cut is the only copy many readers see; put the point there.
A first line that teases and hides the topic. The caption is read as search text as well as feed copy; name the subject in line 1.
Pasting the Reel voice-over as the caption. Say something the video does not: the number, the source, the next step.

sources.title: Instagram Platform: IG User Media reference
sources.supports: caption 2200 chars, 20 @ tags (and the older 30-hashtag figure)

sources.title: Instagram Help: Use hashtags on Instagram
sources.supports: hashtags are tappable and lead to hashtag pages; cap of 5 per post

limits.quote: Maximum 2200 characters, 30 hashtags, and 20 @ tags.
Maximum 2200 characters, 30 hashtags, and 20 @ tags.

cards.formatting: Line breaks render, so a blank line between beats works for phone reading [UNVERIFIED: general platform knowledge, not read from a platform page on 2026-10-04]. Links in a caption are not clickable [UNVERIFIED: general platform knowledge, not read from a platform page on 2026-10-04]. Hashtags are tappable and open a page of posts with that tag (Instagram Help, 'How do I use hashtags?', seen in a search result 2026-10-05); @mention tappability in captions stays [UNVERIFIED: general platform knowledge, not read from a platform page on 2026-10-04]. No native bold or italic in captions [UNVERIFIED: general platform knowledge, not read from a platform page on 2026-10-04]. Emoji are allowed; no source read says how emoji or Devanagari characters are counted toward the 2,200, so leave a margin.
writing_notes: Binding limits (Meta developer reference): 2,200 characters including spaces, and 20 @ tags per caption. `pcw.py check --platform plat:instagram_caption` tests both: the 2,200 characters and the 20 @ tags.
The 20 @ tags limit is counted on the draft: the tool counts @handles (`--field mention` tests that row alone).

Where the hook lands: no official figure for where the feed folds a long caption behind 'more' was found, so none is recorded here and none from a blog should be trusted. Write line 1 as a complete sentence that names the subject and the payoff and still works if it is the only line shown.

Hashtags: write to 5 at most, placed after the last line of copy, chosen as topic + audience + place (for example #GSTIndia #D2CFounders #Jaipur). Do not move the overflow into the first comment: the Help Center says a comment with more than 5 tags will not post (plat:instagram_comment).

Discovery leans on words, not tags (trend:hashtags_to_keywords): put the phrase a person would type, such as 'GST notice ka reply kaise karein', in line 1 and repeat it in the on-screen text or on slide 1.

Hinglish in Roman script is the native register for Indian brand captions; keep one script per caption and do not mix Devanagari and Roman for the same sentence. Sources do not say how Devanagari counts, so for Devanagari or emoji-heavy captions stay under about 2,000 characters and confirm in the composer.
Sponsored or creator posts: the disclosure goes in the first line or the Paid partnership label, not the tail (comp:meta_branded_content, comp:asci_influencer).
Craft shape that works inside the cap: line 1 hook with the keyword, 2-5 short lines of value (one idea, one proof), one CTA verb (save, share, DM 'GST'), then the tags.

algorithm_notes.note: Instagram's December 2025 guidance, as reported by Social Media Today: using 'fewer (up to 5) more targeted hashtags' can improve performance. Third-party report, not an Instagram page.
Third-party summary: since 10 July 2025 Meta lets Google and Bing index public posts from professional Instagram accounts, so caption wording works as searchable text.

Instagram says (April 2026, via Social Media Today) it no longer recommends photos and carousels from aggregator accounts, and an account whose most posts in 30 days are re-posts is treated as an aggregator. Write original captions; credit the source and add your own take on curated posts.

cards.name: Instagram carousel post
cards.summary: One feed post holding several photos and videos people swipe through, with one caption and one comment thread for the whole post. Both routes allow 20 items: the app, and the Graph API that schedulers use. Slide 1 is the only slide shown in the feed.
use_for: Teach-in-slides posts: a step-by-step explainer, a checklist, a myth-versus-fact set
Case-study or before/after sequences for a brand or service business
A government scheme or policy explained in plain-language slides for an Indian audience
Repurposing an article into slides with new copy written for the format (trend:original_content_ranking)
avoid: Filling 20 slides because the app allows it. The limit is a ceiling; cut any slide that does not change what the reader knows.

Planning more slides than the client's publishing tool takes: the app and the Graph API both allow 20 (Meta reference, read 2026-10-20), but ask which route the client uses and confirm a scheduler's own cap before you plan the count.
A weak slide 1. It is the only slide that appears in the feed, so a title card with no promise wastes the post.
Mixing orientations. One orientation applies to every slide.
Cropping article paragraphs onto slides. Rewrite for the format; Instagram deprioritises re-posted material (trend:original_content_ranking).

sources.title: Instagram Help: Share multiple photos or videos as a single post
sources.supports: up to 20 items in the app; one caption and one comment thread for the whole post

sources.title: Instagram Platform: IG User Media reference
sources.supports: API carousels up to 20 items (read 2026-10-20; 10 when first read on 2026-10-04)

limits.quote: You can share a post with up to 20 photos and videos as a single post, also known as a carousel, to your Instagram feed.
Carousels can have up to 20 total images, videos, or a mix of the two.

cards.formatting: One caption and one comment thread cover the whole post (Instagram Help). One orientation applies to every slide (harvest note). In the feed only the first slide shows, with dots below. Caption formatting and limits are those of plat:instagram_caption (line breaks render [UNVERIFIED: general platform knowledge, not read from a platform page on 2026-10-04]; links in captions not clickable [UNVERIFIED: general platform knowledge, not read from a platform page on 2026-10-04]). Slide text is part of the image or video, so it does not count toward any character limit, and the platform cannot search it as caption text [UNVERIFIED: general platform knowledge, not read from a platform page on 2026-10-04].
writing_notes: Which number: 20 per carousel, both in the app and through the Graph API (Meta reference read 2026-10-20; it said 10 when first read on 2026-10-04). If the client publishes through a scheduler, confirm the tool's own cap.
`pcw.py check` cannot count slides (they are images, not draft text), so it tests nothing on this card. Check the caption against plat:instagram_caption and count slides by hand.
Slide 1 is the hook: one promise in large type, the audience named, the keyword they would search. Example: 'GST notice aaya? 5 steps before you reply'.
One idea per slide, 12-25 words on screen as a drafting default (not a platform rule), written for a phone held at arm's length. Hinglish headlines are fine; keep the same script on every slide.
Last slide: one action only (save this, send it to your CA, DM the word 'GST'). Do not stack follow, like, share and link.
The caption does a different job from the slides: line 1 repeats the searchable phrase, then a two-line recap for people who never swipe, then at most 5 hashtags (plat:instagram_hashtags).
Because the whole carousel shares one comment thread, plan the first comment (a pinned clarification or source line) before posting; see plat:instagram_comment.

algorithm_notes.note: Instagram says (April 2026, via Social Media Today) it will no longer recommend photos and carousel posts from aggregator accounts in Explore and other surfaces. Carousels built from other people's material need your own added value.

cards.name: Instagram comment
cards.summary: A comment under a post or Reel, including the creator's own first comment: at most 5 @mentions, hashtags capped at 5 in practice (the comment-error page still prints 30), and the same comment cannot be posted repeatedly, emoji included.
use_for: Brand replies to customer questions and praise
The creator's or brand's first comment: a clarifying line, a source, credits, a keyword prompt
Short call-outs to collaborators (up to 5 @mentions)
Replies that move a complaint to DM with one public acknowledgement
avoid: Moving hashtags into the first comment to dodge the post cap. The hashtag page caps a post at 5 and warns that more than 5 means the comment will not post. Write to 5.
Pasting the same reply to many commenters. Instagram rejects repeated identical comments, even emoji-only ones; vary the wording by starting from the person's actual point.
More than 5 @mentions in one comment; the comment fails.
Canned corporate replies ('Thank you for your valuable feedback'). Answer the specific question in the first sentence.
Writing words Instagram filters. Certain words and phrases are filtered and the comment may not appear; rephrase rather than retry.

sources.title: Instagram Help: I get an error when trying to add a comment
sources.supports: max 5 @mentions, max 30 hashtags per comment, no duplicate comments

limits.quote: You can't include more than 5 @mentions
You can't include more than 30 hashtags in a single comment.
limits.confidence: high (Instagram Help Center; see conflict note)

cards.formatting: Plain text with @mentions (max 5) and hashtags. Repeated identical comments are rejected, including repeated emoji. Instagram filters certain words and phrases. No character limit for a comment is recorded on this card (none was harvested); keep replies short regardless. Whether links in comments are clickable is [UNVERIFIED: general platform knowledge, not read from a platform page on 2026-10-04].
writing_notes: Which hashtag number to trust: the comment-error page (help.instagram.com/161863397286564) still says 30; the hashtag page (help.instagram.com/351460621611097) says 5 and that a comment with more will not post. Write to 5, because the cost of the wrong guess is a comment that silently fails.

`pcw.py check --platform plat:instagram_comment` counts both rows on the comment: @mentions against 5 and hashtags against 30 (`--field mention` or `--field hashtag` tests one). The 30 is looser than the 5 hashtags to write to: test the 5 by running `--platform plat:instagram_hashtags` on the same file.

Reply pattern: answer in sentence 1, name the person or the point they raised, add one concrete next step, stop. Match the commenter's script: Hinglish in Roman for Hinglish comments, Devanagari for Devanagari.
First comment is for what the caption cannot hold: a source line, credits ('Shot by @name'), a pinned FAQ answer. It is not a second caption and not a hashtag dump.

Complaints: one public line that acknowledges and names the next step ('Sorry about this, Riya. Check your DMs, we have your order number'), then take details to DM. Never post personal details in a public reply.
Giveaway and tag-a-friend prompts belong in the caption; keep any @mentions in your own replies to people who consented to be tagged.

cards.name: Instagram hashtags per post or Reel
cards.summary: One Instagram post, Reel or carousel may carry 5 hashtags. Instagram's Help Center says so (read live 2026-10-04), and a post over the cap will not post. The API reference still prints the old figure of 30, so write to 5 and let the caption words do the discovery work.
use_for: Choosing the 3-5 hashtags for a caption, Reel or carousel
Deciding which keywords belong in the caption's own sentences instead of a tag line
Briefing schedulers and freelancers who still carry the old 30-tag habit
avoid: A 30-tag block: it breaks the current cap. The API reference's '30' is the older figure; write to 5.
Generic mega-tags (#viral, #reels, #instagood) as the discovery plan. Use specific tags, topic + audience + place.
Spending two of five slots on two spellings of one idea (#GST and #gstindia). Pick one per idea.
Putting the overflow in a comment. The same cap applies and the comment will not post (plat:instagram_comment).
Leaving discovery to tags alone. Put the searchable phrase in the first line of the caption and in the on-screen text.

sources.supports: cap of 5 hashtags per post

sources.title: Instagram Platform: IG User Media reference
sources.supports: older figure: 30 hashtags per caption

limits.quote: You can use up to 5 tags on a post. If you include more than 5 tags on a single photo/video, your comment won't post.
limits.confidence: high (Instagram Help Center, read in the live page 2026-10-04)

cards.formatting: Hashtags are tappable and lead to a page of posts with that tag (Instagram Help). They can sit in the caption or in comments (Instagram Help, via search result 2026-10-05). Cap is 5 per post (Instagram Help Center); the Graph API reference still prints 30 per caption.
writing_notes: Hard rule: 5 per post (Instagram Help, read live 2026-10-04); a post over 5 will not post. The Graph API media reference still says '30 hashtags'; the Help Center is current. A scheduler built on the API page may accept 30, so write to the Help Center rule anyway.
`pcw.py check --platform plat:instagram_hashtags` counts #tags in the draft against 5. This is the one Instagram card where the count check is exact.
Pick 3-5: one topic tag, one audience tag, one place tag, and at most one campaign or brand tag. Example for a Jaipur CA firm: #GSTNotice #D2CFounders #JaipurBusiness #CALife.
Place tags after the last line of copy so they never push the hook out of the first line.
Hindi or Hinglish: choose the spelling the audience types and use one form per idea; a Devanagari tag and its Roman twin are two slots for one idea.
Move the discovery weight into words: line 1 of the caption, on-screen text and the spoken line should carry the phrase a person would search (trend:hashtags_to_keywords).

algorithm_notes.note: Instagram guidance reported by Social Media Today (Dec 2025): 'Using fewer (up to 5) more targeted hashtags, rather than many generic ones, can improve both your content's performance and people's experience on Instagram.' Third-party report; the cap itself is on Instagram's Help page.
Third-party summary: Meta has let Google and Bing index public posts from professional Instagram accounts since 10 July 2025, which is why caption keywords matter.

cards.name: LinkedIn Sponsored Content ads (single image, carousel)
cards.summary: Paid LinkedIn feed ads. Single image ads take introductory text (150 characters visible, 3,000 maximum), a headline (70 visible, 200 maximum) and a description (100 visible, 300 maximum); carousels take 2-10 cards and intro text of 150 visible and 255 maximum. Write to the visible numbers, not the maximums.
use_for: Lead-gen single image ads for B2B offers (a Jaipur CA firm offering GST notice handling to D2C finance heads)
Promoting a webinar, report or event registration to a job-title audience
Carousel ads that walk through a product, a process or a case study, one claim per card
Promoting a founder's or company's strongest organic post as a sponsored ad
avoid: Writing to the 3,000-character maximum. LinkedIn's own guidance is 150 characters including spaces, emojis and punctuation to avoid truncation; the offer must be inside them.
Relying on the description. It only displays when the image is under 200 px wide or on the LinkedIn Audience Network, so the intro and headline must carry the ad alone.
Pasting a long tracking URL in the intro. URLs over 23 characters are converted to a short link; keep the click-through URL in the ad's destination field.
Using more than 10 emojis in the intro; and in B2B copy even 10 is too many.
Writing organic-post copy. A sponsored ad has three fields with hard visible lengths; organic LinkedIn posts belong to plat:linkedin_post.

sources.title: Single image ads advertising specifications - LinkedIn Marketing Solutions Help
sources.supports: intro text, headline, description, carousel limits

limits.quote: Use up to 150 characters including spaces, emojis, and punctuation to avoid truncation (3,000 character maximum).
Use up to 70 characters to avoid truncation (200 character maximum).
Use 100 characters to avoid truncation (300 character maximum).
You can use up to 10 emojis.
Introductory text - Use up to 150 characters to avoid truncation on some devices (a maximum of 255 characters)
Use a minimum of two cards and a maximum of ten cards.

cards.formatting: Intro text, headline and description are separate fields with visible-length guides (LinkedIn Marketing Solutions Help). Emojis allowed, maximum 10 in the intro, and they count toward characters. URLs longer than 23 characters in the intro are converted to a short link. Description shows only when the image is under 200 px wide or on the LinkedIn Audience Network. Carousel: 2-10 cards; card headlines truncate after two lines. No source read on line breaks, bold or hashtags in ad intro text [UNVERIFIED: general platform knowledge, not read from a platform page on 2026-10-04].
writing_notes: Which number to trust: the 'visible' figures (150 intro, 70 headline, 100 description) are what readers see without truncation; the maximums (3,000, 200, 300) are only what the system accepts. Write to the visible figure.

`pcw.py check` enforces nothing here without --field (five rows). Run `--field headline` (or `--field description`, or `--field "introductory text (single image)"`: a bare `--field "introductory text"` also matches the carousel row and asks you to name one) on a file holding only that field, and read the 'visible before truncation' line it prints; the fail line fires at the maximum, so the real test is whether the 70 or 150 visible characters stand alone.

Intro: the first 150 characters (spaces, emoji and punctuation included) carry the hook and the offer. Example: 'Notice from the GST department? Our CAs reply within 48 hours. Free 15-minute review.' (85 chars).
Headline (70 visible): the outcome or the offer as a noun phrase, no clever wordplay. Example: 'GST notice replies by practising CAs' (36 chars).
Description (100 visible) is a bonus line: proof or a qualifier, never the only place a key fact appears.
Carousel: intro still 150 visible (255 maximum); each card one claim; card headlines fit two lines; minimum 2 and maximum 10 cards; last card holds the single CTA.

Count Devanagari and emoji with margin: LinkedIn says emojis count, and no source read says how Devanagari is counted. B2B LinkedIn ads in India are normally English; use Indian specifics (Rs, crore, GST) in that English.
Check the ad against LinkedIn's advertising policies before launch (comp:linkedin_ads_policy) and against ASCI for claims (comp:asci_code).

cards.name: LinkedIn article (and newsletter edition)
cards.summary: LinkedIn's long-form publishing tool, standalone or as a newsletter edition. No length limit was found on any LinkedIn Help page for the headline, body, newsletter name or newsletter description; the only numbers are for search results: SEO title truncated above 60 characters, SEO description suggested at 140-160.
use_for: Thought-leadership articles under a founder's or expert's name
Newsletter editions that build a LinkedIn subscriber list
Long versions of a post that outgrew the 3,000-character post limit
Evergreen explainers meant to be found in search as well as the feed
avoid: Reading 'no limit' as 'write long'. Length follows the idea; a 700-word piece with one clear point beats 2,500 words of survey.
Leaving the SEO title and description at defaults. They are the only text search engines show; set them in the SEO settings.
An SEO title over 60 characters; LinkedIn Help says it will be truncated.
Publishing the article with no promoting post. The post that shares it needs its own hook (plat:linkedin_post).
Pasting a company brochure under a personal name. Personal-brand articles carry a point of view in the person's own words (genre:thought_leadership_article).

sources.supports: SEO title truncated over 60 chars; SEO description 140-160 suggested

sources.title: LinkedIn Help: Write and publish articles on LinkedIn
sources.supports: article publishing (no length limit stated)

limits.field: SEO title (truncated in search results above)

limits.confidence: medium (LinkedIn Help, last updated about 3 years before 2026-10-04)

limits.quote: We suggest utilizing keywords, summarizing your writing, and aiming to write between 140-160 characters.
limits.confidence: medium (LinkedIn Help, a recommendation not a hard cap, page about 3 years old)

cards.formatting: Confirmed against LinkedIn Help (a522427, read 2026-10-05): you can change the style, bold or italicise text, add ordered or unordered lists, blockquotes and a divider; add images or video, add links, embed content (a LinkedIn post, a member profile, a LinkedIn Page or external content), add a cover image or video, and @mention a member or Page. Heading levels are reached through the style menu; the page does not list the levels. The SEO title and description replace the article title and opening lines only in search-engine results (LinkedIn Help: SEO settings). Devanagari rendering and exact link behaviour in articles are [UNVERIFIED: general platform knowledge, not read from a platform page on 2026-10-04].
writing_notes: Only two numbers exist: SEO title 60 characters (truncated above that) and SEO description 140-160 characters (a recommendation, not a hard cap). The LinkedIn Help page for these is about three years old, so confidence is medium; check how the title looks in a search preview.

`pcw.py check --platform plat:linkedin_article --field "SEO title"` tests the SEO title (60 chars) against the whole file (without --field nothing is enforced), so put only the SEO title in the file. Test the description with `--field "SEO description"` on a file holding only that line.

SEO title: keyword first, under 60, written separately from the headline. SEO description: 140-160 characters that summarise the piece and include the keyword. Example: 'A Jaipur CA explains how D2C founders should answer a GST notice, with a 5-step reply checklist and deadlines.' (110 chars).
Headline and body have no recorded limit. Use sub-headings (style menu), short paragraphs, one blockquote for the claim worth remembering, and an embed or image only where it adds evidence.
Newsletter edition: the newsletter name and description have no recorded limit either; write the description as one sentence that says who it is for and what arrives each time.
Open with the situation or the claim, not the topic: 'Last quarter a Surat exporter lost Rs 4 lakh to a missed notice deadline' (only with facts the client confirms).
No source says how Devanagari is counted toward the 60 and 160; keep a margin if the SEO fields are in Hindi.
Do not state LinkedIn ranking rules as fact; cite LinkedIn's own post or say unconfirmed (trend:linkedin_creator_economy).

algorithm_notes.note: LinkedIn engineering's post on its rebuilt feed, as reported by PPC Land (March 2026): 'The ranking model relies on professional signals and engagement patterns, and specifically excludes demographic attributes.' Third-party report of the LinkedIn post; do not extend it into specific rules.

cards.name: LinkedIn Conversation Ads (sponsored messaging)
cards.summary: Sponsored messaging: a choose-your-path conversation. An intro message of up to 8,000 characters (LinkedIn's composer flags anything over 500) with up to 5 CTA buttons of 25 characters each; one button must be 'Not Interested' and it counts toward the five.
use_for: Webinar and event invitations with 'Register' and 'Send me the recording' paths
Lead-gen conversations that branch to a demo booking, a case study or a checklist
Delivering a gated asset (report, template) with a single clean opt-in step
Follow-up messages that qualify a lead through a button choice, not a form
avoid: Writing toward 8,000 characters. LinkedIn's composer shows a feedback recommendation above 500 because fewer characters can drive higher engagement; treat 500 as the ceiling and aim far lower.
Using all five buttons for offers. 'Not Interested' is required and takes one, so you have four.
CTA labels over 25 characters including spaces and punctuation; they are rejected.
Fake familiarity ('Hi Rohan, I saw your profile') when the message is a mass send. Say why this audience is getting it.
Heavy HTML or rich-text formatting. It counts toward the 8,000.

sources.title: Conversation ads advertising specifications - LinkedIn Help
sources.supports: message, CTA and footer limits

limits.quote: Use up to 8,000 characters, including spaces, emojis, and punctuation.
Call-to-action (CTA) button text | Use up to 25 characters, including spaces and punctuation.
Five CTA buttons per message and 50 buttons per conversation.
You can use up to 10 emojis in the Intro message field.
Use up to 20,000 characters, including spaces and punctuation.

cards.formatting: Intro message up to 8,000 characters including spaces, emojis and punctuation; up to 10 emojis in the intro. HTML and rich-text formatting count toward the 8,000. CTA buttons: 25 characters each, 5 per message, 50 per conversation; 'Not Interested' is required and counts as one of the five. Custom footer and terms up to 20,000 characters. No source read on line breaks or bold in the intro [UNVERIFIED: general platform knowledge, not read from a platform page on 2026-10-04].
writing_notes: `pcw.py check` enforces nothing here without --field (four rows); `--field intro` tests the 8,000, which will pass anything. Test button labels with `--field "CTA button text"` on a file holding only one label, and read the 500-character composer recommendation yourself.
Design the conversation as a tree before writing: intro, up to four real buttons, one required 'Not Interested', then a follow-up message for each button with its own copy.
Intro structure: line 1 says why this person is receiving it (their role or topic), line 2 gives the one offer with a number, then the buttons carry the action.
Button labels are verbs with the outcome, 25 characters or fewer, for example 'Book a 15-min call' (18 chars), 'Send me the checklist' (21 chars), 'Not interested' (14 chars).
Keep the intro in plain sentences; formatting costs characters. English with Indian specifics (Rs, crore, GST) is the usual B2B register on LinkedIn.
Check the offer against LinkedIn's advertising policies before launch (comp:linkedin_ads_policy).

cards.name: LinkedIn document (PDF carousel) post
cards.summary: A LinkedIn post with an uploaded PDF, PPT, PPTX, DOC or DOCX that readers page through, the format people call a carousel. Limits: 300 pages, 100 MB, one million words, and 3,000 characters of post text above it. The document does not carry the post: the text above it needs its own hook.
use_for: Founder or expert carousels: a framework, a checklist, a teardown in one idea per page
Case-study decks and results summaries for B2B buyers
Lead magnets shared as a document with a comment-to-get prompt
Book summaries and portfolio write-ups where the pages are the product
avoid: Reading the 300-page limit as a target. Nobody pages through 300 pages; cut to the pages that change what the reader knows.
Letting slide text do the hook. The post text above the document still needs a first line that works alone.
Small body text. The document is read on a phone; if a page needs a magnifier, split it.
Hindi or Hinglish slides exported without the font embedded in the PDF, so Devanagari shows as boxes. Export to PDF with fonts embedded and open the file on a phone before uploading.
Re-using the same document text as the post text. Say what the document is and what the reader gets, in a different sentence.

The character limit for a post is 3,000 characters.

Text on the pages is read inside the viewer, so it is not part of the post text. Post text above the document follows plat:linkedin_post (3,000 characters; line breaks render [UNVERIFIED: general platform knowledge, not read from a platform page on 2026-10-04]). That the first page shows as the cover before the reader swipes is [UNVERIFIED: general platform knowledge, not read from a platform page on 2026-10-04].

Post text: line 1 says what the document is and the payoff ('12 GST notice replies, one page each'), line 2 gives the reason to open it, then one CTA (comment 'GST' to get the editable version). No official figure for the 'see more' fold exists (see plat:linkedin_post), so the first two lines must stand alone.
Page 1 states the promise; each following page holds one idea in large type; the last page holds one action and the author's name or handle.
Plan page count from the idea, not the cap. A teardown that needs 8 pages should be 8 pages.
Write for the viewer, not for print: 6-8 words of headline per page and a short supporting line, as a drafting default, not a platform rule.
Original content only: rewrite article material for the format (trend:linkedin_creator_economy describes LinkedIn growing as a creator platform; consistent point of view beats recycled lists).

cards.name: LinkedIn post (member or Page)
cards.summary: A text post from a member or a LinkedIn Page: 3,000 characters at most, and past that LinkedIn tells you to write an article. LinkedIn publishes no official figure for where the feed folds a post behind 'see more', so the first two lines have to work as the whole post.
use_for: Ghostwritten founder and executive posts with a point of view
Company Page announcements, hiring posts and event recaps

Hindi and Hinglish Pins: write the title and description in the script and spelling people type when searching; test both on one Pin rather than mixing in a single field.
Link: the exact post or product page, up to 2,048 characters; avoid redirect chains.

algorithm_notes.note: Pinterest Pin specs page: 'Descriptions do not appear when viewing the Pin in the home feed or search feed.' A search summary of that page adds that descriptions are used by the algorithm to determine relevance; that second part was not confirmed on fetch.

cards.name: iOS push notification (Apple Push Notification service)
cards.summary: A remote notification (alert title, subtitle and body) delivered to iPhone, iPad, Mac and Watch through Apple's push service. The payload may be up to 4,096 bytes (5,120 for VoIP); Apple sets no separate character limit on the title or body.
use_for: Order, delivery and booking updates
Cart and re-engagement reminders for D2C and fintech apps
Onboarding nudges and feature announcements
Time-bound alerts such as a payment due date
avoid: Treating 4,096 bytes as a writing budget. The payload limit is generous; the constraint is the lock-screen line a person reads in a second. Write the title and first words to carry the message.
Quoting third-party 'iOS title 50 characters' rules as platform limits. Apple documents no character limit for the alert title or body.
Counting characters when the limit is in bytes. UTF-8 stores each Devanagari code point in 3 bytes and most emoji in 4 or more, so Hindi and emoji copy uses the budget faster.
Forgetting that everything in the JSON payload counts toward the 4 KB, including keys, badge and custom data.

sources.title: Generating a remote notification - Apple Developer Documentation
sources.supports: payload size limits, alert keys

limits.quote: For all other remote notifications, the maximum payload size is 4 KB (4096 bytes).
limits.confidence: high (Apple developer docs; JS page read as markdown through the r.jina.ai reader)

cards.formatting: Alert fields: title, subtitle, body (Apple developer documentation). The whole JSON payload counts toward 4,096 bytes (5,120 for VoIP notifications). Apple documents no separate limit on alert title or body length; what shows depends on the device and the way the notification is displayed. Text is UTF-8, so each Devanagari code point takes 3 bytes and most emoji 4 or more. No markdown or HTML in the alert text [UNVERIFIED: general platform knowledge, not read from a platform page on 2026-10-04].
writing_notes: `pcw.py check --platform plat:push_notification_apns` counts the UTF-8 bytes of the draft file against 4,096. It sees only your text, not the JSON keys, badge or custom data, so leave headroom for those.

What is visible is not documented as a character count (Apple's page states none; third-party figures are not recorded). Write so any truncation costs the least: subject or action first, detail after.

Craft shape: title = who or what (the order, the person, the deadline), body = the one next step with a specific. Example title 'Order #4821 is out for delivery' (31 chars), body 'Arriving today, 4-6 pm. Keep Rs 1,299 ready for COD.' (52 chars).

Hinglish in Roman script keeps byte counts low and reads fast; Devanagari is 3 bytes per character, so a Hindi body of 100 characters is about 300 bytes. Fine against 4,096, but check that the font renders on the lock screen.
Pair this card with genre:push_notification for the craft; the platform gives you a payload cap and no copy limit, so the discipline is yours.

cards.name: Push notification via Firebase Cloud Messaging (Android, iOS, web)
cards.summary: A title-and-body notification delivered through Firebase Cloud Messaging to Android, iOS and web users. The API payload may be up to 4,096 bytes; messages sent from the Firebase console are limited to 1,000 characters. Neither FCM nor Android documents a hard title or body character limit; what is visible depends on the device, the OS and whether the notification is expanded.
use_for: Transactional alerts: order, delivery, payment and booking updates
Re-engagement and cart-reminder pushes for Android-first apps
Onboarding nudges that move a new user to the next step
Announcements sent from the Firebase console to a segment
avoid: Quoting a '40-50 character title' rule as if it were platform documentation. Those figures come from push blogs, not FCM or Android, and are not recorded here.
Sending a console message over 1,000 characters. The console enforces that cap even though the API allows 4,096 bytes.
Writing for one device. Test collapsed and expanded states on a low-end Android and an iPhone before sending to a large list.
Counting characters when the API limit is bytes. In UTF-8 each Devanagari code point uses 3 bytes and most emoji 4 or more.

cards.formatting: Notification messages and data messages share a 4,096-byte maximum payload (Firebase docs). The Firebase console enforces a 1,000-character limit. Visible length depends on device, OS and whether the notification is expanded; no hard title or body limit is documented. Text is UTF-8. Markdown or HTML in notification text [UNVERIFIED: general platform knowledge, not read from a platform page on 2026-10-04].

The platform gives no visible-length figure, so write the title as a complete thought in a few words and the body so its first clause makes sense alone; whatever the device cuts is then the least important part.
Do not repeat the app name in the title; the OS shows the app name beside the notification (check on a device).

Craft shape: title = the thing that changed, body = the one next step with a specific. Example title 'Your refund of Rs 840 is processed' (34 chars), body 'It reaches your bank in 2-3 working days. Tap to see the details.' (65 chars).
Hinglish in Roman script is compact and reads naturally; Devanagari costs 3 bytes a character but is well within 4,096. Test font rendering on low-end Android devices.
Pair with genre:push_notification for copy craft; the platform limit is a ceiling, not a target.

cards.name: RCS Business Messaging (Google RBM)
cards.summary: Google's RCS Business Messaging: branded rich messages in the Android Messages app. A text message holds up to 3,072 characters; a rich card has a title of up to 200 and a description of up to 2,000; suggestion chips are 25 characters each, up to 11 per message; carousels hold 2-10 rich cards.
use_for: Order and delivery updates as a rich card with action chips
A product carousel of 2-10 cards with a reply or action on each
Appointment reminders with 'Confirm' and 'Reschedule' chips
Short promotional messages where an image and buttons beat plain SMS
avoid: Writing it like SMS. The text limit is 3,072 characters and a rich card holds an image, a title, a description and up to 4 suggestions; use the format.
Suggestion text over 25 characters, or more than 11 suggestions in one message.
Assuming Latin-character budgets for Hindi or emoji copy. The guide says emoji and multi-byte characters count as 2-4 or more, so Devanagari consumes the budget faster.

Assuming India's commercial-messaging rules do not apply. Indian RCS business traffic may also fall under TRAI commercial-communication rules; this was not checked here (comp:trai_tcccpr_2018, plat:sms_india_dlt).
Putting one long block of text in a card description just because 2,000 characters are allowed.

`pcw.py check --platform plat:rcs_business_messaging --field "text message"` tests the text limit (3,072 chars) in visible characters (without --field nothing is enforced), which is lower than Google's count for emoji and Devanagari. Test chips with `--field suggestion`, card title with `--field "rich card title"`, description with `--field "rich card description"`, one element per file.

Devanagari and emoji: the guide says multi-byte characters count as 2-4 or more. If counted as UTF-8 bytes a Devanagari character is 3, so a 25-limit chip may hold only about 8 Devanagari characters. That is an inference, not a documented rule; confirm with a test message on a test device and keep Hindi chips short.
Chips are verbs with the outcome in 25 characters or fewer: 'Track order' (11 chars), 'Reschedule' (10 chars), 'Talk to an agent' (16 chars).
Message design: line 1 says who it is from and why now; one purpose per message; put the image, title and a one-line description in a rich card and the action in a chip.
Carousel: 2-10 cards with parallel copy (same pattern of title, one-line benefit, one action) so scanning is easy.
Indian use: check the sender registration and consent rules before sending commercial RCS traffic (comp:trai_tcccpr_2018 applies to SMS; this card has not verified how it applies to RCS).

Choosing a subreddit name
Writing the sidebar rules, FAQ and resources widget

Community name: 3-21 characters, cannot be edited after creation (Reddit Help: How to create a community). Description pattern: one sentence on who the community is for, one on what to post, one boundary (what is not welcome). Example: 'For Indian D2C founders to ask and answer questions on GST, shipping and cash flow. No self-promotion links.' (108 chars).
Name: 3-21 characters, permanent; choose the word members would type, short and spellable. Check that it is not just a brand name unless it is a brand community.
Sidebar text widget (markdown): a few rules in a numbered list, a short FAQ, links to resources. Keep it scannable; most people read only the top.
If the client is a brand running the community, say so in the description or the first sidebar line, and never use fake accounts to fill it (trend:reddit_and_forums_in_search says do not astroturf).
Match the language of the community: an English-language India community may still welcome Hinglish; say so in the rules if it does.

cards.name: Reddit post (title + text body)
cards.summary: A Reddit submission: a title of up to 300 characters (no markdown) and an optional text body of up to 40,000 characters (80,000 with Premium, since the November 2025 change) written in Reddit markdown. Each subreddit adds its own title, body and flair rules.
use_for: Discussion, question and answer posts in niche communities
AMAs, case-study write-ups and 'what we learned' posts that a community can verify
Community announcements and feedback threads in a brand-run subreddit
Detailed answers that become the thread people find through search
avoid: Posting before reading the subreddit's rules and top threads. Rules differ by community and posts are removed for promotion, flair and format.
A link as the whole post. Write the full answer or context in the body.
Undisclosed brand posting. Say 'I work at <brand>' in the first line.
Pasting the same post across many subreddits.
Markdown in the title. Titles do not render markdown.
Clickbait titles. State the question or finding with its specifics.

cards.formatting: Title: up to 300 characters, does not render markdown (Reddit API docs). Body: Reddit markdown, which renders bold, italic, headings, lists, links, tables and spoilers (Reddit Formatting Guide, per the harvest note). Body limit 40,000 characters for non-Premium users and 80,000 for Premium (Reddit Help). Each subreddit may add its own title and body rules and flair. Test the body with `--field "text body"` (it matches both body rows and asks you to name one: `--field 'text body (non-Premium)'` tests 40,000, `--field 'text body (Premium)'` 80,000).
Title: say the question or the finding with a specific (city, price, time frame, version). Example: 'How are Jaipur D2C brands handling a GST notice for a mismatch in GSTR-1 and 3B?' (80 chars).

Body: context first (who you are, what you tried), then the question or the findings, then what you want from readers. A short TL;DR at the top of a long post is a community habit, not a platform rule.
Disclose affiliation in the first line when you represent a brand or sell something, and keep the tone of a member, not a pitch (trend:reddit_and_forums_in_search).
Add one detail readers can verify (a price band, a time frame, a source link where the rules allow). Do not argue with critics; acknowledge the point and add the fact.
Read the subreddit rules, the pinned post and the top threads of the month before drafting; some communities require flair or ban links.
Language: match the community. An India-focused subreddit may accept Hinglish; do not assume it, read recent threads.
